Academic misconduct can be identified by staff involved in marking or teaching.
In cases of suspected cheating, further investigative work (i.e. discussion with the student about how they completed the work) may be necessary to determine if cheating may have occurred.

process.quote: have a supportive discussion with the unit director, or another appropriate staff member on ways of working and expectations of academic integrity
convene a panel to investigate the academic misconduct:
If academic misconduct is suspected, the case is investigated and considered under one of the following procedures:
The student may elect not to attend an interview and to submit a statement to the panel instead.
The student is notified in writing of the suspected case (including the pieces of work affected) and invited to interview with a panel.
Where the student does not attend an interview, unless prevented by unforeseeable circumstances, the panel proceeds to reach its conclusions without the student’s attendance.
The student may be accompanied by another person at the panel interview.
The student has the usual right of appeal against a decision of the Exam Board and, in the case of expulsion, the decision of the Dean of the Faculty.
The student is informed of the panel’s decision within two weeks of the date of the panel.
the panel determines if, on the balance of probabilities, misconduct has occurred or not.
A case is held on a student’s record for future internal reference in case further concerns over academic misconduct are raised.

outcomes.quote: Providing it is a first offence of this nature and the case is not considered too serious, no further assessment is needed and support is provided to the student to prevent future occurrences,
the work in question is awarded a mark of zero.
